quests.trigger: An unaccompanied minor requests rations at a ruin crossing.
quests.discovery: A child sits against the concrete with their coat pulled over their knees, too tired to stand up for you. 'Do you have any food?' They ask it the way you ask about the weather, because they have asked it a lot.

choices.label: Give all your food
choices.outcome_text: You hand over everything you are carrying. They eat half, fast, and put the rest inside their coat. Then they give you a charcoal drawing of a house, because they think a trade is polite.
choices.epitaph: Gave the child everything in the pack. Came away with a drawing of a house.

choices.label: Give half your food
choices.outcome_text: They eat slowly and keep both eyes on your hands the whole time, in case the rest of it is coming.
choices.epitaph: Split my rations with the child at the crossing. Kept enough to walk home on.

choices.label: Give a little food
choices.outcome_text: A crust changes hands. It buys them the afternoon, and they know it, and they say thank you anyway.
choices.epitaph: Left the child a crust. It bought an afternoon, not a week.

choices.label: Refuse and walk on
choices.outcome_text: You shake your head. They pull the coat back over their knees and go still again, saving what they have left for whoever comes next.
choices.epitaph: Walked past a hungry child at the crossing. Kept my own supply whole.

quests.trigger: A family of four is found sheltering in an abandoned apartment block.
quests.discovery: Two adults, two children, in a stairwell they have hung blankets across. The mother is holding an infant that has not made a sound since you came in. 'We have not eaten in a week,' the father says, flatly, as though the number is the only part he trusts himself with.

choices.label: Give all your supplies
choices.outcome_text: You empty the pack onto the blanket. The father does not thank you; he starts dividing it into four piles and then, after a moment, into five, and pushes one back toward you.
choices.epitaph: Emptied the pack in a stairwell for a family of four. They tried to give a share back.

choices.label: Give half your supplies
choices.outcome_text: Half of what you carry stays on the blanket. They portion it out before you are through the door, and the children are made to eat first.
choices.epitaph: Left half my stores with the family in the stairwell. Children ate first.

choices.label: Give a little
choices.outcome_text: You set a few tins inside the doorway. The mother says a name you do not catch, twice, and it takes you a street and a half to work out that it was thanks.
choices.epitaph: Left a few tins in the doorway. It buys them days, not weeks.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.outcome_text: You tell them you have nothing to spare. The mother nods as though she had already priced that answer in. The father swears at you, once, and does not look up again.
choices.epitaph: Told a starving family I had nothing spare. It was not entirely true.

quests.trigger: A man with a compound fracture lies in an alley.
quests.discovery: A man is down in the alley with the bone through the skin above his knee. He has a belt round his thigh and he has done a competent job of it. 'Help me,' he says, and then, more quietly, 'before dark.'

choices.label: Give medical supplies
choices.outcome_text: You splint it against a length of pipe and use most of the bandages. He talks the whole time about what he will owe you and where to find him, which is how he keeps from screaming.
choices.epitaph: Splinted a stranger's leg in an alley. He insists he owes me.

choices.label: Give food instead
choices.outcome_text: No bandages to spare, so you leave food and water within reach. It steadies him. The leg is still broken when you go.
choices.epitaph: Left food with the man in the alley. Left the leg as I found it.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You keep to the far wall as you pass. He stops asking a few paces before you are out of earshot, which is worse than if he had not.
choices.epitaph: Passed the man in the alley. Kept the medical kit sealed.

choices.label: Take his supplies
choices.outcome_text: You take his pack. He gets a hand to the strap and cannot hold it, and after that he only watches you do it.
choices.epitaph: Took the pack off a man who could not stand up to stop me.

quests.trigger: A severely dehydrated traveler enters your camp perimeter.
quests.discovery: The traveller stops at the line without being told to, swaying, lips split, tongue too dry to shape more than the one word. 'Water.' They hold their empty canteen up so you can see through it.

choices.label: Give all your water
choices.outcome_text: You hand over your canteen and they drink it dry in one go, then sit down hard. When they can talk again they draw you a map to a spring that runs clean, and make you repeat the turnings back to them.
choices.epitaph: Gave a stranger my whole canteen. Traded it for the way to clean water.

choices.label: Give half your water
choices.outcome_text: You pour off half. They ration it in sips without being asked, which tells you how long they have been out here.
choices.epitaph: Poured off half my water at the perimeter. Enough to keep them walking.

choices.label: Give a sip
choices.outcome_text: A capful, no more. They look at the level in the canteen, then at you, and decide not to say the thing they were going to say.
choices.epitaph: Spared a capful at the perimeter. We both knew what it was worth.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.outcome_text: You put the canteen away where it cannot be seen. They nod once and walk on south, at the same pace, which is the only pace they have left.
choices.epitaph: Turned a thirsty traveller away from the line. They walked on south.

quests.trigger: An elderly survivor in terminal decline requests company and rations.
quests.discovery: An old woman sits propped against a wall with her bag squared off beside her, breathing in a rhythm that keeps losing its place. 'I haven't long,' she says. 'But I'd take a voice, if you've got one to spare.'

choices.label: Give food and medicine
choices.outcome_text: You spend rations and medicine on someone who will not need them long. She talks for an hour, mostly about her sister, and at the end of it tells you where the family shelter is and which key opens it.
choices.epitaph: Spent food and medicine on a dying woman. She left me her family's door.

choices.label: Give some supplies
choices.outcome_text: You leave what you can afford at her side and stay while she eats some of it. She is careful to say your name back to you before you go.
choices.epitaph: Left supplies with the old woman by the wall. Stayed while she ate.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You sit with her and give her nothing else, because there is nothing else. She says that is what she asked for, and means it, and does most of the talking.
choices.epitaph: Sat with a dying woman and gave her nothing but the hour.

choices.label: Take her supplies
choices.outcome_text: There is almost nothing in the bag, and you take it. She does not have the air in her to argue, so she just watches you go through it.
choices.epitaph: Went through a dying woman's bag. It held almost nothing.

quests.trigger: A woman in active labor arrives at an abandoned medical outpost.
quests.discovery: A woman is braced in the doorframe of the outpost, counting under her breath between contractions. 'They're getting closer together,' she says. 'It's coming here, whatever we do about it.'

choices.label: Give all your medical supplies
choices.outcome_text: You put everything sterile you own on the table and boil what you cannot. It takes most of the night, and it works: a small, furious, breathing baby. She asks what you are called, and gives the child your name to carry.
choices.epitaph: Emptied the whole medical kit on a delivery in the dark. The child has my name.

choices.label: Give some supplies
choices.outcome_text: Enough antiseptic for hands and cord, and clean cloth, and no more. It is not how anyone would choose to do it, and both of them come through.
choices.epitaph: Gave up antiseptic and clean cloth for a field delivery. Both came through.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You keep the kit closed. She goes inside on her own and gets on with it in the dark, and you are down the road before you find out how it ended.
choices.epitaph: Kept the kit shut and left her to it. Never learned how it ended.

choices.label: Take her supplies
choices.outcome_text: You take her bag while she is on her knees in the doorway. She screams at you until a contraction takes the voice out of it, and you keep walking through both.
choices.epitaph: Took a labouring woman's bag off her. She screamed until she couldn't.

quests.trigger: A wounded hostile combatant with an inoperable weapon requests aid.
quests.discovery: A raider is down in the dirt with a burst receiver on the rifle beside them and a hole in them that is going to finish the job the rifle didn't. 'Gun's dead, I'm dead, so.' They spread the empty hand. 'Quarter. Asking properly.'

choices.label: Give medical supplies
choices.outcome_text: You pack the wound and strap it. They watch you work, decide you are worth paying, and give you their crew's patrol times for the next nine days.
choices.epitaph: Patched a raider who asked for quarter. Bought their crew's patrol times.

choices.label: Give food
choices.outcome_text: No bandages, just food. They eat it one-handed and fast, and never once stop watching the road behind you.
choices.epitaph: Fed a bleeding raider instead of patching them. They ate watching the road.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You stay well out of reach and give them nothing. They try to spit at you and do not have the pressure for it.
choices.epitaph: Left a raider in the dirt where I found them. Gave nothing.

choices.label: Finish them
choices.outcome_text: You finish it. The last thing they do is tell you, with something like satisfaction, that their crew keeps a list and you are on it now.
choices.epitaph: Killed a raider who had asked for quarter. Their crew keeps a list.

quests.trigger: An ambushed Peacekeeper operative is incapacitated on a primary route.
quests.discovery: A Peacekeeper is propped against a burnt-out chassis, uniform torn open at the thigh, that leg no good at all. They give it to you the way they were trained to: 'Ambushed at the bend, four of them, two hours ago. My people will come. I need to still be here when they do.'

choices.label: Give all your supplies
choices.outcome_text: You work the leg and leave them everything you can carry out without. They pay in the only currency they have on them: safehouse ciphers, patrol frequencies, and a name to use at any of their posts.
choices.epitaph: Kept a Peacekeeper alive at the bend. Came away with their ciphers and a name to use.

choices.label: Give some supplies
choices.outcome_text: Enough to stop the bleeding and steady them. They thank you formally, note your description for the record, and start dragging themselves toward the ridge line rather than wait.
choices.epitaph: Stabilized a Peacekeeper and moved on. They chose not to wait for pickup.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You keep walking. They do not call after you, and they do not stop looking at you either, all the way down the road, memorising the shape of whoever you are.
choices.epitaph: Walked past a downed Peacekeeper. They watched me the whole way out.

choices.label: Take their supplies
choices.outcome_text: You strip their kit. They get one hand into your sleeve and hold on longer than you would expect a man with that leg to manage, and it still is not enough.
choices.epitaph: Stripped a wounded Peacekeeper's kit. Their people will hear my description.

quests.trigger: A Knowledge Keeper with compromised optics reports caloric deficiency.
quests.discovery: An archivist sits over a radio that has not worked in years, glasses mended at the bridge with copper wire and held on at an angle. 'I can't read past arm's length any more,' they say, 'and I've been three days on boiled paper. In that order of importance, I'm afraid.'

choices.label: Give food and spare glasses
choices.outcome_text: Food first, then the spare lenses. They put them on, look at the far wall for a while without saying anything, then read you a pre-war survey of the whole valley and press the document into your hands.
choices.epitaph: Fed the archivist and found them lenses. They gave me a survey of the valley.

choices.label: Give food only
choices.outcome_text: You leave food and no lenses. They recite coordinates from memory instead, checking each one twice against a ledger they can no longer see.
choices.epitaph: Fed the archivist. Wrote down the coordinates they knew by heart.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You leave them with an empty shelf, an empty stomach, and a room that is getting further away from them every week.
choices.epitaph: Left the archivist to the dark and the boiled paper.

choices.label: Take their notes
choices.outcome_text: You take the survey notes. They come after you as far as the doorway, grabbing at the pages, making a sound you would expect from someone being cut.
choices.epitaph: Took the archivist's notes. They came after me as far as the door.

quests.trigger: A local warlord who previously granted safe passage is cataloging ammunition.
quests.discovery: The warlord who waved you through last winter is sitting by a low fire pit sorting brass into tins by calibre. He does not get up. 'You went through my ground once and came out the other side. Let's find out what that was, you and me. Habit, or an arrangement.'

choices.label: Give them supplies
choices.outcome_text: You put the supplies down by the tins. He looks at what you brought, not at you, and says the road stays open, and it does.
choices.epitaph: Paid the toll to the warlord by the fire pit. The road stayed open.

choices.label: Give them nothing
choices.outcome_text: You tell him no. He goes back to sorting brass without any change in his face, which is somehow more of an answer than shouting would have been.
choices.epitaph: Refused the warlord's toll to his face. He only kept sorting brass.

choices.label: Take their supplies
choices.outcome_text: You go for what he has. He finds this funny, and lets you back out of the camp anyway, which costs him nothing and costs you the arrangement.
choices.epitaph: Tried to rob the warlord. He laughed and let me leave.

quests.trigger: A radiation-compromised specialist requests pharmaceutical intervention.
quests.discovery: A specialist sits inside a ring of hand-drawn decay curves, coughing into a rag that has stopped being white. She is clinical about it, because that is her training and it is all she has left. 'Acute exposure, about three weeks in. I need chelators. I have work to trade for them.'

choices.label: Give all your medicine
choices.outcome_text: You hand over the whole medicine roll. Once she can hold a pen she writes out a chelation schedule better than anything your shelter has, and then keeps writing until the light goes.
choices.epitaph: Gave a dying specialist all my medicine. She wrote out a treatment schedule worth more.

choices.label: Give some medicine
choices.outcome_text: You give her part of the roll. It buys her steady hands for an afternoon, which she spends copying the formula onto a support beam in grease pencil, high up, where damp will not reach it.
choices.epitaph: Split my medicine with the specialist. She left the formula on a beam.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You keep the roll. She accepts it without argument and returns to the charts, which are, you realise on the way out, all charts of herself.
choices.epitaph: Kept my medicine. Left the specialist working out her own numbers.

choices.label: Take their research
choices.outcome_text: You take the binder out from under her hands. She gets half a curse out before the coughing takes the rest of it, and she is still coughing when you are out of the building.
choices.epitaph: Took the binder from a dying specialist. Left her coughing over the empty table.

quests.trigger: A soil engineer assesses completely compromised crop rows.
quests.discovery: The soil engineer is on his knees in the row with a handful of grey dirt, letting it run out through his fingers and catching it again. 'Nothing in it. Not poisoned, just dead. Give me live seed and something to feed it and I can bring this back. Otherwise we're standing in a graveyard with a fence round it.'

choices.label: Give seeds and fertilizer
choices.outcome_text: You hand over live seed stock and the chemical feed to go with it. He works out your share on the spot, aloud, twice, and writes two-fifths of every harvest against your name where the others can see it.
choices.epitaph: Gave live seed and feed to the sterile rows. Two-fifths of the harvest is mine on paper.

choices.label: Give some supplies
choices.outcome_text: Part of the seed, part of the feed. He revises his numbers down without complaining about it and writes you a share proportional to what you actually gave.
choices.epitaph: Gave what seed I could spare. My share was written down honestly.

choices.label: Give nothing
choices.outcome_text: You look at the rows, and at the man in them, and go on your way. He is still sifting the same handful when you reach the fence line.
choices.epitaph: Left the dead rows to the man kneeling in them.

choices.label: Steal their seeds
choices.outcome_text: You take what seed they have left, which is not enough to plant and not enough to eat. He follows you to the fence, shouting, and after that they will know your face here.
choices.epitaph: Took the last seed off a failing farm. They chased me to the fence.

quests.trigger: An elderly survivor offers civic infrastructure schematics disguised as anecdotes.
quests.discovery: An old man feeds a small fire one splinter of board at a time, patient as a teller counting coins. 'I planned this city. Forty years of pipes and culverts,' he says. 'I only tell it as stories. You'll have to sit through the stories.'

choices.label: Hear the story
choices.outcome_text: You sit through a story about a water main and the winter it burst. In the middle of it, without changing tone, he gives you the way into an intact bunker under the east junction.
choices.epitaph: Sat through an old man's stories. He gave me the way into a bunker.

choices.label: Stay for all of it
choices.outcome_text: You stay until the fire is down to coals and he is down to the names of people who signed off on things. At the end he tells you about a second cache, a small one, that nobody ever came back for.
choices.epitaph: Stayed for every story he had. He trusted me with a cache nobody else claimed.

choices.label: Cut him off
choices.outcome_text: You stop him in the middle of a sentence about a storm drain. He nods once, like a man used to it, and does not say another word to you.
choices.epitaph: Cut an old man off mid-sentence. He didn't say another word to me.

choices.label: Tell him his city is gone
choices.outcome_text: You tell him the city is ash and his maps are a tour of nowhere. He feeds the last splinter to the fire, and whatever he was saving for a listener, he keeps for good.
choices.epitaph: Mocked an old man's life work. He kept the rest of his stories to himself.

quests.trigger: A woman rocks a cradle no one sleeps in.
quests.discovery: A woman sits by a cold stove, rocking a cradle with nothing in it, her foot keeping a rhythm her hands have nothing to do with. A mended shirt, far too small for anyone here, lies folded on her knee. 'She would have been five this winter,' she says, not quite to you. 'I still cut the bread small.'

choices.label: Sit with her
choices.outcome_text: You sit on the floor near the stove and stay while she talks, some of it about the girl and some of it about nothing at all. When the rocking finally slows, she wraps a small wind-up toy in a cloth and puts it in your hands, and does not explain it, and you do not ask.
choices.epitaph: Sat with her until the talking ran out. Came away with a toy meant for smaller hands.

choices.label: Stay, but keep quiet
choices.outcome_text: You take the chair and say nothing, not one word. She rocks, and mends, and after a long while her hands stop hurrying. That is all that happens, and it is enough for her.
choices.epitaph: Kept quiet in her room until the room settled. Nothing got fixed.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.outcome_text: You go back out the way you came. Behind you the cradle keeps its rhythm, steady as a clock nobody is reading.
choices.epitaph: Left a woman rocking an empty cradle. Kept my day on schedule.

choices.label: Tell her the cradle is empty
choices.outcome_text: You tell her she is spending strength on an empty box. The sound she makes is not loud, but it carries, and soon there are shapes at the far edge of the light that were not there before.
choices.epitaph: Told her the rocking was a waste. Her answer brought company neither of us wanted.

quests.trigger: A former combatant offers an unsolicited after-action report.
quests.discovery: A soldier works a whetstone along a knife that is already sharp, one stroke at a time, in no hurry to finish. 'Requesting an audience for an after-action report of the Exchange,' they say. It is not a question, and the stone does not stop.

choices.label: Accept the debrief
choices.outcome_text: You take the whole report, contact by contact, the way they need to give it. When the last name is accounted for, they pick up your rifle, check the sights against their thumbnail, and put right what the road knocked loose.
choices.epitaph: Sat through the full after-action report. My rifle shoots true again.

choices.label: Cross-examine the report
choices.outcome_text: You press the gaps: who held the stairwell, when the water gave out, why the flank folded. They correct the record out loud as they go, and the version you walk away with is the one that holds.
choices.epitaph: Picked holes in their report. The holes were real, and what was left was worth having.

choices.label: Decline the report
choices.outcome_text: You tell them no, not today. They nod once, and the whetstone picks back up at the same even pace, as if you had never stopped by.
choices.epitaph: Declined a soldier's report. The sharpening went on without me.

choices.label: Mock their unit
choices.outcome_text: You laugh at how their unit folded and offer the report back as comedy. The knife comes off the stone, and the next minute costs you blood and bandages before it lets you go.
choices.epitaph: Made a joke of a unit's last stand. Got corrected at knifepoint.

quests.trigger: A child wants to tell someone what the stars are for.
quests.discovery: A kid grabs your sleeve with both hands, too wound up to be polite about it. 'Can I tell you about the stars? I figured out what they're for,' they say, and they are already telling you.

choices.label: Hear the whole theory
choices.outcome_text: You crouch down and take the whole theory, every planet and comet of it, in order. When it is over they draw you a map of the sky on paper scrap and write your name on a cluster, because now it belongs to you.
choices.epitaph: Heard a kid's whole theory of the stars. There's a paper sky somewhere with my name in it.

choices.label: Nod along
choices.outcome_text: You say 'go on' and 'is that so' at the right places, and it is enough. They go off glowing, already improving the theory for the next person.
choices.epitaph: Nodded through a kid's star theory. It made their whole day.

choices.label: Tell them not now
choices.outcome_text: You say you don't have time for stars. They let go of your sleeve like it went cold and drift back to their corner.
choices.epitaph: Told a kid I had no time for stars. They let go of my sleeve.

choices.label: Tell them the stars are gone
choices.outcome_text: You explain that the sky is buried and the stars are a guess about something no one can see. They don't argue. They just go quiet in a way that takes the theory with it.
choices.epitaph: Proved to a kid that the sky is ash. They stopped talking about stars.

quests.trigger: A former medical officer wishes to detail their triage protocol failures.
quests.discovery: A field surgeon works solvent into a pair of forceps that has been clean for some time. 'The first week, I ran triage by the book,' they say to the wall. 'I need to say the black-tag names where somebody can hear them.'

choices.label: Hear the names
choices.outcome_text: You stay for all of it, every name and the reason after it, until the solvent rag dries out. When the list is done they sit lighter in the chair, and they give you a small key and tell you which pharmacy's lockbox it fits.
choices.epitaph: Heard every black-tag name read out loud. Left with the key to a pharmacy lockbox.

choices.label: Tell them the math held
choices.outcome_text: You tell them the numbers were the numbers, that the book was the only thing standing between some and none. Their breathing comes easier after that. Neither of you says it made anything right.
choices.epitaph: Told the surgeon the math was sound. Neither of us called it right.

choices.label: Decline the confession
choices.outcome_text: You say you can't carry it for them. They take it like they have heard it before, and go back to cleaning instruments that were already clean.
choices.epitaph: Declined to hear the names. The forceps got cleaner.

choices.label: Blame them for the black tags
choices.outcome_text: You tell them a real doctor would have found a way to save more. They set the forceps down very carefully, and from then on their door is shut to you, whatever you are bleeding.
choices.epitaph: Told the surgeon they should have saved everyone. I don't get treated there anymore.

quests.trigger: A self-appointed chaplain offers a doctrinal broadcast on the Exchange.
quests.discovery: A figure in ash-grey vestments plants themselves in your path, hands folded like the end of a service. 'Friend,' they say, 'will you hear what the fire meant? Someone ought to say it, and someone ought to hear it.'

choices.label: Hear the sermon
choices.outcome_text: You stand through the whole sermon, fire and judgment and the short roll of the saved. They take your stillness for devotion, and at the end they lay a hand on your weapon and ask the ash to pass it by.
choices.epitaph: Stood through the whole sermon. They blessed my weapon like I was one of theirs.

choices.label: Argue the theology
choices.outcome_text: You take the doctrine apart piece by piece, and they light up like it is a festival day. No one has argued with them in a long while. You part on good terms and no agreement.
choices.epitaph: Argued doctrine with the chaplain. Best talk they'd had in months.

choices.label: Walk past
choices.outcome_text: You step around them and keep walking. The sermon carries on behind you without a pause, addressed now to nobody at all.
choices.epitaph: Walked around the chaplain. The sermon didn't need me.

choices.label: Threaten them quiet
choices.outcome_text: You tell them the next word of scripture gets answered in kind. They go quiet, and they mark you down as one of the things the fire was sent to test.
choices.epitaph: Threatened a preacher into silence. I hear I'm in the sermons now, as a warning.

quests.trigger: An engineer wants to detail the exact failure mode of the local bridge.
quests.discovery: An engineer stands at the foot of the collapsed overpass, turning a sheared bolt over in their fist like a coin. 'The rebar went from thermal shock, not the blast,' they say. 'Everyone says the blast. Give me ten minutes and the concrete will tell you the truth.'

choices.label: Follow the math
choices.outcome_text: You walk the span with them, twist by twist, until the failure reads like a sentence you could recite. Satisfied that someone finally checked their work, they tell you about a maintenance level underneath that nobody else remembers.
choices.epitaph: Walked the overpass and heard out the math. Now I know the way into the maintenance level.

choices.label: Take their word for it
choices.outcome_text: You nod through the equations without checking a line of them. It does not matter; a witness was the whole requirement. They chalk the last number on the concrete and stand up lighter.
choices.epitaph: Nodded through the engineer's math. They only needed it witnessed.

choices.label: Skip the lecture
choices.outcome_text: You leave them talking to the concrete and pick your own way over the rubble. It takes longer than it should, and you never do learn why.
choices.epitaph: Skipped the lecture. Crossed the rubble the slow way.

choices.label: Blame them for the bridge
choices.outcome_text: You say the bridge fell because people like them built it cheap. The sheared bolt leaves their hand before the sentence lands. It goes wide by a foot, which is its own kind of answer.
choices.epitaph: Told the engineer their kind built it cheap. They threw a bolt at me and missed.

quests.trigger: A frightened survivor blocks the road with a warning about the ash.
quests.discovery: A survivor plants themselves in the middle of the road, hands shaking, eyes on the sky instead of on you. 'Don't take the low road,' they say. 'There's something in the ash. I've seen it move. Somebody has to write it down.'

choices.label: Hear the warning out
choices.outcome_text: You stand there and let them get it all out: the shapes, the timing, which road. Once it is said to someone who didn't walk off, they steady enough to press a homemade filter mask on you, the good kind of crude.
choices.epitaph: Heard the whole warning, every mad word. Left with a filter mask that works.

choices.label: Ask for proof
choices.outcome_text: You ask what they saw, exactly, from where, and for how long. They have nothing that would hold up anywhere else, and they know it, but being questioned like it mattered leaves them grateful anyway.
choices.epitaph: Pressed them for proof. They had none, and thanked me for asking.

choices.label: Wave it off
choices.outcome_text: You call it a fever dream and step around them. They don't argue. They just turn back to the sky and go on watching it for both of you.
choices.epitaph: Waved the warning off as madness. Somebody's still watching the sky.

choices.label: Shove past them
choices.outcome_text: You put them down in the road and step over. By the time they are back on their feet, you are in their bookkeeping, filed somewhere between the shapes in the ash and worse.
choices.epitaph: Put a frightened person in the dirt to save a minute. I'm on their list now.

choices.label: Mock their fear
choices.outcome_text: You laugh at them and take the road they feared, loudly. The road takes the joke badly.
choices.epitaph: Mocked the warning and walked right in. Paid for the joke.

quests.trigger: A survivor by a fire tells of love before the exchange.
quests.discovery: A woman feeds photographs to the fire one at a time, not burning them, warming them. 'He used to bring me flowers. Before everything changed,' she says.

choices.label: Listen sympathetically
choices.outcome_text: You hear it through. At the end she gives you the last photograph, kept whole. 'Someone should carry it forward.'
choices.epitaph: Heard her whole story. She gave me the last photo to carry forward.

choices.label: Listen politely
choices.outcome_text: You nod at the right beats. She keeps one photograph and lets you see it.
choices.epitaph: Listened to the lover's tale. She showed me the last photo.

choices.label: Interrupt or leave
choices.outcome_text: You leave her to the photographs.
choices.epitaph: Left her to her photographs. The fire was doing its slow work.

choices.label: Laugh at the romance
choices.outcome_text: You laugh at flowers. She stands up. The night rearranges itself.
choices.epitaph: Laughed at the flowers. She stood up and the night changed shape.

quests.trigger: A former teacher offers a lesson on the world before.
quests.discovery: A woman with cracked glasses and a straight back looks you over. 'You could use some education. Let me tell you about the world before,' she says, and it starts exactly on time.

choices.label: Listen attentively
choices.outcome_text: Hours pass like minutes. You leave reading the signage on the dead roads.
choices.epitaph: Sat through the teacher's whole lesson. I can read the road signs now.

choices.label: Listen, but bored
choices.outcome_text: You fidget through half. She assigns you homework: a sign to read on your way out.
choices.epitaph: Half-listened to the lesson. She left me homework. I did it.

choices.label: Interrupt or leave
choices.outcome_text: You've survived this long without the old world. You go.
choices.epitaph: Walked out of the schoolroom. Survived fine. Know less.

choices.label: Mock her teaching
choices.outcome_text: You tell her the old world is dead weight. She closes the book gently, like a coffin lid.
choices.epitaph: Mocked the teacher's old world. She closed the book on me.

quests.trigger: You catch a young thief with your gear, and an explanation.
quests.discovery: A young man freezes with your flashlight halfway into his coat. 'I can explain. I was going to pay you back,' he says fast, and mostly means it.

choices.label: Hear the explanation
choices.outcome_text: His sister is coughing somewhere. You listen, then let him keep the light. He becomes useful after that.
choices.epitaph: Heard the thief out. Let him keep the light. He's been useful since.

choices.label: Listen, skeptical
choices.outcome_text: You question the story. Half of it holds. He returns half of what he took.
choices.epitaph: Questioned the thief's story. Half held up. Half came back.

choices.label: Report them to the camp
choices.outcome_text: You hand him to the watch. The camp handles it. His sister's cough handles itself.
choices.epitaph: Turned the thief in. The camp was thorough. I didn't stay to learn the rest.

choices.label: Take more from them
choices.outcome_text: You take from him what he took from you, plus interest. He doesn't argue. He remembers.
choices.epitaph: Took back my gear and then some. He didn't argue. He'll remember.

quests.trigger: A wild-eyed man says the stars speak to him.
quests.discovery: A wild-eyed man points at the smoke-stained sky like it owes him money. 'The stars speak to me! Want to hear their message?' he asks, urgent as weather.

choices.label: Hear the vision
choices.outcome_text: The vision is nonsense stitched with coordinates. You use the coordinates. They're real.
choices.epitaph: Heard the prophet's vision. The message was madness with a map in it, and the map was real.

choices.label: Listen skeptically
choices.outcome_text: You sort the signal from the noise with him. Half the message survives your doubts, and half of that is useful.
choices.epitaph: Argued the prophet's vision into sense. Kept the parts that held.

choices.label: Interrupt or leave
choices.outcome_text: You have messages of your own to deliver, to anywhere but here.
choices.epitaph: Left the prophet to his stars. They talk only to him.

choices.label: Mock the visions
choices.outcome_text: You laugh at the stars. He goes very still and says your name, which you never gave him.
choices.epitaph: Mocked the prophet's stars. He said my name. I never gave it.

quests.trigger: A woman has just buried her partner in the yard.
quests.discovery: A woman sits beside a mound of turned earth with her hands folded in her lap, not looking at it. 'He went quiet in the night,' she says. 'I kept waiting for him to complain about the cold, the way he always did.'

choices.label: Sit with her
choices.outcome_text: You sit down in the dirt next to her and stay. Nothing gets better while you are there. When the light starts to go, she stands, pulls his coat off the pile, and puts it in your arms. 'It's a good coat. He'd be angry if it went in the ground.'
choices.epitaph: Sat with a woman beside fresh earth. Came away wearing her partner's coat.

choices.label: Say it out loud
choices.outcome_text: You say the word she has been not-saying. She nods once, like she had been waiting for someone to let her believe it, then goes back to her shelter and starts rolling her bedding.
choices.epitaph: Told a woman her partner was dead because she needed to hear it. She packed before dark.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.outcome_text: You keep walking. The mound gets smaller behind you, and then the turn of the path takes it.
choices.epitaph: Walked past a woman sitting with fresh dirt. Kept the hour for myself.

choices.label: Tell her the sitting costs her
choices.outcome_text: You price it for her, the daylight, the calories, the cold coming in. She says nothing, but she memorizes your face, and you both know what for.
choices.epitaph: Priced a woman's grief out loud. She filed my face away for later.

quests.trigger: A child screams through a nightmare in the sleeping quarters.
quests.discovery: A kid is thrashing on a sleep mat, fists knotted in the blanket, heels drumming the floor. 'They're coming in! They're over the wire!' he shouts, still asleep.

choices.label: Wake him slowly
choices.outcome_text: You say his name from a step back until he comes up out of it. He stares at the walls a long time, checking them. Before you leave he presses a folded scrap into your hand, a map of where he has seen salvage, to pay for the waking.
choices.epitaph: Talked a kid up out of a nightmare. He paid me in a salvage map.

choices.label: Shake him awake
choices.outcome_text: You grab his shoulder and shake hard. He comes up gasping and stays rattled for an hour afterward, but the quarters are quiet.
choices.epitaph: Shook a kid awake to stop the screaming. He shook longer than he had screamed.

choices.label: Let him sleep it out
choices.outcome_text: You turn over and face the wall. The shouting burns itself down to whimpers, then to nothing.
choices.epitaph: Let a kid scream himself down. It stopped on its own.

choices.label: Order him quiet
choices.outcome_text: You tell him to shut it or he'll be out in the cold alone. The screaming stops. So does everything else in him, he doesn't look at anyone for two days.
choices.epitaph: Frightened a kid into silence. He stayed quiet after that.

quests.trigger: A badly wounded survivor is slipping into shock.
quests.discovery: A man is folded around a gut wound at the side of the path, breathing in small sips. He has stopped making noise. That is worse than the noise was.

choices.label: Keep talking to him
choices.outcome_text: You crouch and keep your voice on him, your name, his name, the weather, anything, and the shock waits a while. Before he goes under he tells you he owes you his life, and to collect if he lives.
choices.epitaph: Talked a gut-shot man through the worst of it. He says he owes me his life.

choices.label: Apply standard first aid
choices.outcome_text: You press the wound closed and bind it tight. The bleeding slows. Whatever is happening behind his eyes is not something a bandage reaches.
choices.epitaph: Bound a man's belly wound. Left the rest of it where I found it.

choices.label: Keep walking
choices.outcome_text: You stay on your route. Shock does not take long in this cold.
choices.epitaph: Left a wounded man to the cold. He had maybe an hour.

choices.label: Shove him aside
choices.outcome_text: You move him out of your path with your boot. He folds up smaller and goes quiet sooner than he would have.
choices.epitaph: Kicked a dying man out of my way. It hurried things.

quests.trigger: A survivor has frozen up in a dark cellar.
quests.discovery: Someone is kneeling in the cellar corner, hands clamped over their ears, rocking. 'It's the quiet,' they get out between breaths. 'I can't breathe in the quiet.'

choices.label: Talk them through it
choices.outcome_text: You sit on the floor where they can see you and keep talking, small dull things, until their breathing evens out some. Nothing is fixed, they are still down there when you leave. Later you find your pack repacked and tidy, the only thanks they could manage.
choices.epitaph: Sat on a cellar floor and talked someone through the dark. They sorted my pack to say thank you.

choices.label: Leave a light
choices.outcome_text: You crack a chem light and set it in the corner. It does not help them breathe, but it gives the room edges.
choices.epitaph: Left a light stick with someone afraid of the dark.

choices.label: Leave them be
choices.outcome_text: You go back up the stairs. The dark and the panic keep each other company.
choices.epitaph: Left someone panicking in a cellar. It wasn't my air they were short of.

choices.label: Bang the pipes
choices.outcome_text: You hit the pipes hard, to see what happens. What happens is they fold in on themselves and stop answering.
choices.epitaph: Rang the pipes beside a frightened person. They went somewhere inside and stayed.

quests.trigger: A survivor is deep in withdrawal.
quests.discovery: A survivor is shaking hard enough to knock their knees together, sweat through their coat in the cold. 'I need it,' they say, working their hands open and shut. 'Just enough to stop the shaking. Then I'll quit, I swear it.'

choices.label: Sit with them through it
choices.outcome_text: You stay through the worst hours, water when they can hold it, a hand on the shoulder when the shaking peaks. Come morning they eat half a ration and keep it down. It is the first day in a long time they end without the drug.
choices.epitaph: Sat up all night with someone coming off the drug. Morning came anyway.

choices.label: Give them a dummy dose
choices.outcome_text: You give them a capsule of flour and call it the real thing. The shaking eases for a while, because the body wants to believe you.
choices.epitaph: Handed a shaking person a pill full of nothing. It worked for an hour.

choices.label: Give them the drug
choices.outcome_text: You give them what they are asking for. The shaking stops almost at once. It will be worse next time, and you have made sure there will be a next time.
choices.epitaph: Gave an addict the drug. Stopped the shaking, started the clock again.

choices.label: Trade a promise for their gear
choices.outcome_text: You promise the dose if they hand over their pack and tools, then you keep walking with both. They are shaking too hard to follow.
choices.epitaph: Traded a lie for everything a sick person owned.

quests.trigger: A survivor cannot stop counting why they lived.
quests.discovery: A survivor sits with a pencil stub and a paper covered in figures, crossing out and starting again. 'Ninety-eight point seven percent of my unit is dead,' they tell you. 'I keep running it. It comes out the same every time.'

choices.label: Tell them someone had to be the one
choices.outcome_text: You tell them that in a dying this size, somebody has to be left over, and it means nothing about them. They sit with that a while. Then they teach you a guarded radio frequency, something useful to carry instead.
choices.epitaph: Told a survivor their living meant nothing either way. They gave me a radio frequency for it.

choices.label: Agree the odds were bad
choices.outcome_text: You agree with them. The odds say they should be in the ground. They nod, write the number down again, and for the first time all night put the pencil down.
choices.epitaph: Agreed with a man that he should be dead. It was what he wanted to hear.

choices.label: Let them keep counting
choices.outcome_text: You leave them to the pencil and paper. Their numbers are not eating your rations.
choices.epitaph: Left a man alone with his arithmetic.

choices.label: Tell them they lived on others' deaths
choices.outcome_text: You tell them their air was paid for with better people. The pencil stops moving. It does not start again while you are there.
choices.epitaph: Told a man his life was bought with the dead. Broke something he needed.

quests.trigger: An old man wants to pass on everything he knows before he dies.
quests.discovery: An old man pats the crate beside him. 'I've got forty years of this place in my head,' he says. 'Floods, filters, which walls sweat first. I need to put it in somebody else before it goes where I'm going.'

choices.label: Listen to all of it
choices.outcome_text: You sit until your legs ache, through flood marks and filter schedules and the names of the dead who taught him. When it is done he gives you his folding knife, good steel, like a receipt for the hours.
choices.epitaph: Sat through an old man's whole archive. He paid me in a good knife.

choices.label: Take only what keeps you alive
choices.outcome_text: You cut him down to the parts that keep a body breathing, water, rot, weather. He gives you the knife anyway, and does not say what he thinks of the shortcut.
choices.epitaph: Took the useful parts of an old man's memory. Left the rest.

choices.label: Tell him you'll manage
choices.outcome_text: You tell him you will learn it the way everyone learns it. He nods and closes his mouth around everything he knows.
choices.epitaph: Refused an old man's lessons. I'll pay for them later, one mistake at a time.

choices.label: Tell him his memory is going
choices.outcome_text: You tell him his head is failing and everyone can see it. He looks at you a moment, then turns the crate so you cannot sit on it.
choices.epitaph: Mocked an old man's memory. He stopped offering it.

quests.trigger: The sleeper next to you is fighting someone in their dreams.
quests.discovery: The survivor on the next mat is at war in their sleep, knuckles cracking against the floorboards. 'Contact left! Wake up, wake up!' they shout at nobody.

choices.label: Wake them gently
choices.outcome_text: You say their name from where their hands cannot reach you, palms open, until they come up out of it. They check the room twice before they believe it. At breakfast they push half their portion your way without a word.
choices.epitaph: Woke a sleeper out of a bad dream. They split their breakfast with me.

choices.label: Jolt them awake
choices.outcome_text: You grab a shoulder and shake. They come up swinging. Afterward they sleep with their back to the wall and one eye on you.
choices.epitaph: Hauled a dreamer awake the hard way. They watch me now.

choices.label: Cover your ears
choices.outcome_text: You pull your coat over your head and keep your own sleep. Their war is not your watch.
choices.epitaph: Slept through someone else's war.

choices.label: Set off a noise beside them
choices.outcome_text: You clap once, sharp, right by their ear, to see what they do. What they do is come up off the mat white and shaking, and they do not sleep again that night.
choices.epitaph: Tested a sleeping person's fear for my own answer. They paid for it.

quests.trigger: A survivor has gone three weeks without a conversation.
quests.discovery: A survivor holds their watch post without moving, and starts talking before you have decided to stop. 'You're the first voice I've had in three weeks,' they say. 'I counted.'

choices.label: Stay and talk
choices.outcome_text: You trade two hours of nothing much, weather, rations, a dog one of you used to know. When you get up to leave they press extra rations on you, as if talk were something you can pay off.
choices.epitaph: Talked two hours with someone starving for it. They paid me in food.

choices.label: Tell them three weeks is normal now
choices.outcome_text: You tell them three quiet weeks is about standard these days. They write it down, like a fact is company.
choices.epitaph: Told a lonely person their loneliness was normal. They wrote it down.

choices.label: Don't stop
choices.outcome_text: You keep moving. Their voice follows you a few steps and then gives up.
choices.epitaph: Walked past three weeks of silence. It reached for me and I kept walking.

choices.label: Tell them talking is a weakness
choices.outcome_text: You point out that a voice carries and the wrong people listen. They nod, shut their mouth, and that is the end of the only conversation they had going.
choices.epitaph: Taught a lonely person that speech is dangerous. Cheap lesson to give.

quests.trigger: A survivor is screaming at the sky.
quests.discovery: A survivor is shouting at nothing, fists up, tendons standing out in their neck. 'IT DOESN'T ADD UP!' they roar at the clouds. 'NONE OF IT ADDS UP!'

choices.label: Wait it out nearby
choices.outcome_text: You stand off at a distance until the shouting wears itself down. Afterward they tell you the whole list of what they lost, every name, like reading a manifest out loud.
choices.epitaph: Stood by while someone screamed themselves empty. Then I heard the whole list of their dead.

choices.label: Talk them down
choices.outcome_text: You keep your voice low and even until theirs drops to meet it. The fists stay clenched. That part you cannot talk away.
choices.epitaph: Talked a scream down to a shout. The anger stayed where it was.

choices.label: Keep your distance
choices.outcome_text: You give them room and let the fire burn its fuel. It goes out the way fires do.
choices.epitaph: Kept clear of someone's breaking point.

choices.label: Agree with them, loudly
choices.outcome_text: You shout back that they are right, it never added up. They turn around and swing at the nearest thing, which is you.
choices.epitaph: Gave an angry person agreement. They paid it back with their fists.

quests.trigger: A survivor wants to rebuild a collapsed structure.
quests.discovery: A survivor unrolls a hand-drawn plan across your knees and weights the corners with stones. 'The east support can go back up,' they say. 'I checked the math twice. It's not impossible. It's just hard.'

choices.label: Tell them it can stand
choices.outcome_text: You go over the drawing and say so, it can stand. Before you are finished saying it you are holding a work detail with your name on it.
choices.epitaph: Told a dreamer the dream would hold. Now I carry stones for it.

choices.label: Look the plan over
choices.outcome_text: You read the whole thing. Some of it would bear weight. You say which parts, and leave the rest unsaid.
choices.epitaph: Read a rebuilding plan. Half of it was true.

choices.label: Wave it off
choices.outcome_text: You don't look at the drawing. Someone else's ceiling is not your problem.
choices.epitaph: Refused to look at a plan for putting a roof back.

choices.label: Tell them what it would cost
choices.outcome_text: You price it out loud, the timber, the hands, the food for the hands. They roll the plan up slowly and do not unroll it again while you watch.
choices.epitaph: Added up a rebuilding job for its author. The plan went back in the tube.

quests.trigger: A survivor has decided the math says they will die.
quests.discovery: A survivor sits with their back to a reinforced wall, hands folded like someone at a desk. 'The calories don't cover the winter and the rads don't care,' they say. 'I ran it every way. I don't come out of this.'

choices.label: Talk about tomorrow only
choices.outcome_text: You don't argue the winter. You argue for tomorrow, one day, that is all anyone has to get through. They agree to that much. It is not hope, but it is a time you both set.
choices.epitaph: Talked a dying arithmetic down to one day. They agreed to the day.

choices.label: Offer the usual words
choices.outcome_text: You say the things people say. They hear each one land and stay where it lands. Nothing moves.
choices.epitaph: Gave a despairing person the standard words. They were worth what they cost.

choices.label: Check their math and go
choices.outcome_text: You read their figures. The arithmetic is honest. You put the paper back in their hand and keep your rations in your pocket.
choices.epitaph: Checked a stranger's death math. It balanced. I kept walking.

choices.label: Tell them they're wasting air
choices.outcome_text: You tell them the air would do more good in someone with a future. They look at you for a while, then stop breathing, sooner than even their own figures called for.
choices.epitaph: Told a dying person they were wasting air. They stopped using it.

quests.trigger: You find a shallow grave in the ash with no marker and no tags.
quests.discovery: A dip in the ash, filled in and packed down by a boot heel. Whoever did it worked fast. No tags, no name, nothing driven into the ground to say who is under it.

choices.label: Mark the grave
choices.outcome_text: You write the coordinates in your log and set a length of pipe upright over the spot, wired to a strip of cloth. The next patrol through here will see it and walk around.
choices.epitaph: Marked a grave that had no name on it. Left the coords in the log so nobody digs there twice.

choices.label: Walk around it
choices.outcome_text: You give the dip a wide berth and keep moving. It is already filled. There is nothing in it that asks anything of you.
choices.epitaph: Walked around a grave with no marker. It was already covered. That had to be enough.

choices.label: Dig it up
choices.outcome_text: You dig for an hour and learn nothing. There is no tag, no papers, nothing to tell you who this was, and you burn the morning doing it.
choices.epitaph: Opened a stranger's grave looking for answers. Found none. Filled it back in with my own hands.

choices.label: Take what was buried
choices.outcome_text: The grave goods are real: a jacket, a belt, a canteen with a dent in it. You take all three. Everything smells of the ground and goes straight into a bleach soak when you get back.
choices.epitaph: Took a jacket, a belt and a canteen off a buried stranger. The canteen still works.

quests.trigger: You find a body caught in a flash fire, burned past recognition.
quests.discovery: Whatever the fire was, it took this person in one pass and went no further. What is left is fused to the floor plates, black and light as charcoal. There is no face to read and no tag that survived.

choices.label: Cover and mark it
choices.outcome_text: You kick down the half-standing partition so it falls over the spot, then paint a stripe on the wall by the door. The dust stays where it is, and the next crew knows not to sweep there.
choices.epitaph: Buried a burned body under its own wall. Painted a stripe so nobody tracks it home.

choices.label: Keep your distance
choices.outcome_text: You cross the room wide of it and go on. Burned that thoroughly, it is not a sickness risk. It is only a thing you have to look at, and you choose not to.
choices.epitaph: Walked past a burned body. There was nothing left to bury that the fire had not already done.

choices.label: Pick through it
choices.outcome_text: Near the edge of the burn you find a belt buckle, a knife in a scorched sheath, a metal flask. The flask's seal held. You take all three and leave the rest fused where it sits.
choices.epitaph: Took a knife and a flask off a burned body. The flask outlived the fire. So did I.

choices.label: Shove it aside
choices.outcome_text: You need the floor space, so you lever the remains off the plates with a bar. They come up in pieces, and the dust gets into your mask filters. You will be tasting it for two days.
choices.epitaph: Moved a burned body with a pry bar because it was in my way. Ruined a set of filters doing it.

quests.trigger: A swollen body is lodged in the intake of a working water source.
quests.discovery: The body is caught against the intake grate, swollen tight against the bars, and the water backs up around it in a slow, scummed pool. This stream feeds three camps. In another day or two it will feed them this.

choices.label: Drag it clear
choices.outcome_text: You rope the ankles and haul from the bank, and it takes most of an hour before the grate runs clean. You wash your arms to the elbow and lose your gloves to it. The downstream camps never hear about any of this.
choices.epitaph: Pulled a body out of the intake. Lost my gloves and my appetite. Three camps drink tomorrow and don't know why.

choices.label: Mark it foul and go
choices.outcome_text: You scratch a warning into the intake post and note it on your map. Your own water is already topped up. The next crew will have to make their own call.
choices.epitaph: Found the intake fouled by a body. Left a warning scratched on the post and kept my own water.

choices.label: Yank it out barehanded
choices.outcome_text: You get impatient and pull it free by the belt. The skin gives at the wrist, something lets go inside, and the splash gets your sleeves and your pack. You spend the evening boiling everything you were wearing.
choices.epitaph: Dragged a swollen body out by the belt with no gloves. Boiled my clothes that night and threw the belt in the fire.

choices.label: Push it downstream
choices.outcome_text: You work it off the grate with a pole and let the current take it. Your water runs clear by evening. Somewhere below, the stream bends through a sector whose name you do not know.
choices.epitaph: Shoved a body off the intake and let the current have it. My water cleared. Someone else's won't.

quests.trigger: You find the skeleton of a small child in a ruined house.
quests.discovery: In the back room of a collapsed row house, a small skeleton lies on its side, arms around a plastic toy truck gone chalky with years. The bones are dry and weightless. Whoever it was, they went to sleep holding the thing they liked most.

choices.label: Bury them with the truck
choices.outcome_text: The ground outside is frozen two knuckles deep, and digging takes you the rest of the daylight and chips your shovel. You put the truck in with them. A scavenger passing on the road stops, watches, and gives you one nod before moving on.
choices.epitaph: Buried a child and a toy truck in frozen ground. Cost me the daylight and chipped the shovel. A stranger nodded at me from the road.

choices.label: Close the door
choices.outcome_text: Bones that dry are no danger to anyone. You pull the door shut behind you and leave the room the way it has been for years.
choices.epitaph: Shut the door on a child's bones. They'd kept this long. They'll keep.

choices.label: Take the truck
choices.outcome_text: The fingers snap like dry twigs when you work the truck free. It is good molded plastic, pre-war, and the trader at the crossing will give you two days of lamp oil for it.
choices.epitaph: Snapped a toy truck out of a dead child's hands. It trades for two days of lamp oil.

choices.label: Sift the room
choices.outcome_text: You go through the room on your knees, moving bones aside to get at the floorboards. There is nothing under them. You leave an hour later with dust on your cuffs and nothing to show for it.
choices.epitaph: Pawed through a dead child's room looking for valuables. There weren't any.

quests.trigger: You find a machine-dug pit filled with layered bodies.
quests.discovery: A pit the length of a bus, cut by a machine in a single day, filled in layers. You can count forty in the top layer alone. The work was fast and organized, done in the first weeks after the exchange, by people who were still following orders.

choices.label: Record it and leave a marker
choices.outcome_text: You walk the edges, pace out the corners, and enter it on your network map as a place to be left alone. You set one of your own rations on a flat stone at the head of the pit. It will be gone by morning, but that is not the point.
choices.epitaph: Paced out a pit of forty or more and put it on the map as ground you don't dig. Left a ration on a stone. Can't say why.

choices.label: Walk the perimeter
choices.outcome_text: The filling was finished years ago. You circle it once, more out of habit than need, and take the road on the far side.
choices.epitaph: Walked around a full pit. The work there was done long before I came.

choices.label: Strip the top layer
choices.outcome_text: The newest bodies still wear. You go down among them and come up with a coat, two pairs of boots laced together, and a wool hat. You do not look at any of their hands. Everything goes into a sealed bag for boiling.
choices.epitaph: Went down into a pit and came up with a coat and two pairs of boots. Didn't look at their hands.

choices.label: Burn the pit
choices.outcome_text: You pour your fuel along the rim and put a flare to it. It burns for hours, and the column of smoke stands straight up in the still air, visible for miles. By dusk you can see a scout drone circling it, and you are no longer alone out here.
choices.epitaph: Burned a mass grave with my own fuel. The smoke brought a drone. Whoever buried them knows someone was here.

quests.trigger: You find a body hanging from a highway gantry.
quests.discovery: The rope is synthetic braid, the knot a trucker's hitch, neat and practiced. That is not a knot a person ties on themselves. The body has been up there long enough that the birds have been and gone.

choices.label: Cut them down and bury them
choices.outcome_text: You climb the gantry, saw through the braid, and lower the body hand over hand. Digging below the roadbed takes the rest of the day. You coil the cut end of the rope and leave it on the grave, because it is theirs and you do not want it.
choices.epitaph: Cut a hanged stranger down off the gantry and put them under the roadbed. Left the rope on the grave. Didn't want it.

choices.label: Keep to your route
choices.outcome_text: The gantry is not on your errand. You pass under it on the far shoulder and do not look up more than once.
choices.epitaph: Walked under a hanged body on the gantry. Looked up once. Kept walking.

choices.label: Cut them down, leave them
choices.outcome_text: You cut the rope from the walkway and let the body drop into the weed strip below, out of the sightline of the road. That is the part the next traveler will thank you for. The ground is frozen anyway, you tell yourself, and keep moving.
choices.epitaph: Dropped a hanged body off the road so the next one through doesn't see it. Ground was too frozen for the rest. That's what I said.

choices.label: Take the rope
choices.outcome_text: Eight meters of good synthetic braid, worth more than your boots. You cut it at the top so you lose almost none of it, and the body drops where it drops. The rope coils into your pack like it was never anyone's.
choices.epitaph: Cut eight meters of good rope off a hanged body. Best salvage this month. That's the whole entry.

quests.trigger: You find a skeleton shut inside a bedroom closet.
quests.discovery: The closet was locked from the inside. A skeleton sits on the floor of it under a good wool coat, knees drawn up, one hand still against the door. They chose the smallest room in the house and pulled it shut behind them, and the house kept them.

choices.label: Carry them out and bury them
choices.outcome_text: You wrap the bones in a bedsheet and dig in the side yard, where the soil is soft from an old garden. The coat goes in too. After, the house is only a house, and you sleep in it without thinking about the closet.
choices.epitaph: Buried the one from the locked closet in the garden soil, coat and all. Slept in the house after. It was just a house.

choices.label: Shut the door again
choices.outcome_text: They sealed themselves in and the seal has held this long. You close the bedroom door on top of it and take your search to the other rooms.
choices.epitaph: Left the one in the closet where they chose to be. Closed two doors on it.

choices.label: Take the coat
choices.outcome_text: You lift the coat off and the skeleton folds in on itself with a sound like sticks settling. The wool is thick, barely worn, and warm the moment you put it on. It will see you through two more winters.
choices.epitaph: Took the wool coat off the one in the closet. Two winters in it, easy. They stopped needing it a long time ago.

choices.label: Burn the closet out
choices.outcome_text: You bar the other doors, splash your fuel in the closet, and set it alight from the hallway. The fire jumps to the room, then the floor above. You stand in the yard and watch the whole house go, which is one way to be sure.
choices.epitaph: Burned a good house down to be rid of one closet. Watched it go from the yard.

quests.trigger: You find a body face-down in a flooded section.
quests.discovery: The water stands waist-deep between two walls, and the body floats face-down in the middle of it, turning slow circles off the current. The swelling has been going for days. Your filter rig can still beat this water, but the margin is narrowing by the hour.

choices.label: Haul it out and bury it
choices.outcome_text: You wade in, get a line under the arms, and drag it up onto the concrete walk. Digging into the rubble fill takes an hour. The water will not get cleaner on its own, but the worst of it is now in the ground instead of in the flow.
choices.epitaph: Waded in and pulled a floater onto the walk, buried it in the fill. The water's still bad. It's less bad.

choices.label: Mark it and move on
choices.outcome_text: You chalk a mark on the wall at both ends of the flooded stretch and note it in the log. Your bottles are full enough to skip this source entirely.
choices.epitaph: Chalked a floater's stretch as foul water and walked on. Had enough in the bottles to afford that.

choices.label: Strip it in the water
choices.outcome_text: You hold it against a half-sunk door and work the belt, the boots, and the synthetic jacket free. Everything comes off slick and foul. The jacket is good under the grime, but you rinse your hands and forearms for a long time after.
choices.epitaph: Stripped a floater in waist-deep water. Kept the jacket. Scrubbed to the elbow and still felt it.

choices.label: Send it downstream
choices.outcome_text: You wade in behind it and shove. The current in the culvert takes hold, and the body slides away through the outfall into the next flooded block. Your stretch of water starts clearing within the hour.
choices.epitaph: Shoved a floater into the culvert. My stretch cleared by dark. The next block gets it instead.

quests.trigger: You find a burn pit where the fire went out too soon.
quests.discovery: A shallow pit lined with scorched brick, and in it bone that the fire only half finished, chalk-white at the edges. Whoever tended this ran out of fuel or out of time. A dented fuel can lies in the weeds, empty, where they dropped it.

choices.label: Finish it by hand
choices.outcome_text: You crush what the fire left with the flat of your shovel and scatter it past the pit, a shovelful at a time, into the wind. It takes the better part of an hour. When the pit is empty you kick the brick lining in after it.
choices.epitaph: Finished a stranger's cremation with a shovel and the wind. Kicked the pit in after. Their fire had quit; mine didn't.

choices.label: Leave the pit
choices.outcome_text: There is nothing left here that can rot or spread. You step around it and keep to your errand.
choices.epitaph: Stepped around a half-finished burn pit. Nothing left in it that could hurt anyone.

choices.label: Sift the ash
choices.outcome_text: Down in the ash your fingers find a ring, tungsten, warped oval by the heat. The scrap man pays by weight and does not ask questions about metal that shape. You pocket it.
choices.epitaph: Sifted a burn pit and found a warped ring. The scrap man pays by weight and doesn't ask.

choices.label: Burn it again
choices.outcome_text: You spend your own fuel on it, a quarter-can you were saving, and stand watch while it burns down properly. Warm work on a cold day. You cannot call it wasted, exactly, but the can is empty and you are still alone out here.
choices.epitaph: Spent a quarter-can of my own fuel finishing a stranger's fire. Can't say it was wasted. Can say the can is empty.

quests.trigger: You find a bound body in a holding cell, shot against the wall.
quests.discovery: The cell door stands open. The body sits against the back wall with its hands still wired in front of it, and the wall behind is pocked in one tight group at head height. This was done slowly, by people with time and a procedure.

choices.label: Cut the wire and bury them
choices.outcome_text: You work the wire off the wrists, carry the body out past the wire fence, and dig where the ground is clear of concrete. It takes the day. You leave the cell block standing open behind you, because nothing in it needs keeping anymore.
choices.epitaph: Cut the wire off a prisoner's wrists and buried them outside the fence. Left the cell open. Nothing there to keep.

choices.label: Leave the cell as found
choices.outcome_text: The cell did its job and the record of it is still sitting against the wall. You close the door the way it was and let the block keep its own account.
choices.epitaph: Closed the cell door on a wired body. The block keeps its own records.

choices.label: Take the boots
choices.outcome_text: Military boots, half a size big, with miles left in the soles. You unlace them off the body and wipe them down on the cell blanket. Your own pair has a split seam you have been wrapping in tape for a week.
choices.epitaph: Unlaced the boots off an executed prisoner. Half a size big. Better than the taped pair I walked in on.

choices.label: Lay them out properly
choices.outcome_text: You have not got the hours for a grave, so you cut the wire, straighten the legs, fold the arms, and set the hands together on the chest. It is not a burial. It is the difference between how they were left and how you leave them.
choices.epitaph: Couldn't spare the digging. Cut the wire and laid the prisoner out with their hands folded. Left them better than I found them. That's all it was.

quests.trigger: You find a body in a sealed room, dead by their own hand.
quests.discovery: The room was taped shut from the inside. The means of it is there on the floor beside the body, plain to see. On the table there is a folded sheet of paper held down by a stone, written full in a careful hand.

choices.label: Bury them with the letter unread
choices.outcome_text: You dig out back, lay the body in, and set the folded sheet on the chest without opening it. Whatever it says, it was not addressed to you. You fill the grave and leave the tape on the door for the next one to find.
choices.epitaph: Buried the one from the sealed room with their letter on their chest, unread. It wasn't written to me.

choices.label: Leave the room sealed
choices.outcome_text: They built this closure themselves, layer by layer. You put the door back as it was and leave the tape to keep holding.
choices.epitaph: Left the sealed room sealed. They arranged it themselves. I just knocked.

choices.label: Write them down as weak
choices.outcome_text: You chalk it on the wall by the stairwell where the floor's residents will read it: room four, gave up, do not mourn. It costs you nothing to write. You tell yourself it is a warning and not a verdict, but the chalk says what it says.
choices.epitaph: Chalked 'gave up, do not mourn' by the stairwell. Told myself it was a warning. The chalk doesn't care what I tell myself.

choices.label: Take their supplies
choices.outcome_text: They went out stocked: two sealed ration bricks, a full canteen, a good flashlight with fresh charge. You take all of it. The flashlight alone is a week's good light, and they clearly stopped counting days.
choices.epitaph: Took two ration bricks and a good flashlight off the one in the sealed room. They'd stopped needing days.

quests.trigger: You enter a block where everyone was killed at once.
quests.discovery: The bodies lie where they fell, in doorways and at the bottoms of stairs, some still holding what they were carrying. It happened fast, in one sweep, by people who knew the block's layout and worked through it in order. Nobody here ran far.

choices.label: Dig a common grave
choices.outcome_text: Two full days of daylight, one long trench in the lot behind the block, and your shovel gives out on the second morning so you finish with a length of shelving. You carry them down one at a time and do not count them. When it is done you pile the dirt high and mark it with a door stood on end.
choices.epitaph: Dug one trench behind the block, two days, broke the shovel, finished with a shelf. Didn't count them. Marked it with a door.

choices.label: Route around the block
choices.outcome_text: You skirt the block on the far sidewalk and mark the corners on your map so you never come through here by accident. The work that was done here is finished, and it was never yours to finish.
choices.epitaph: Walked around a block where everyone died at once. Drew it on the map so I never cut through by mistake.

choices.label: Work the block for salvage
choices.outcome_text: You go doorway to doorway, room by room, and take what the sweep left: canned goods under a cot, a solar charger, three pairs of good shoes, a toolkit still latched. It fills two packs. You are efficient about it, and you do not learn any of their names.
choices.epitaph: Worked a dead block room by room. Two full packs out of it. Didn't learn any names. That was deliberate.

choices.label: Burn the block
choices.outcome_text: You set fires at four corners and let the wind do the rest. The smoke stands over the block all afternoon, and by evening there are lights on the ridge that were not there before, held steady on you. You leave in the dark, the long way home.
choices.epitaph: Torched a dead block to be done with it. The smoke brought watchers to the ridge. Went home the long way in the dark.

quests.trigger: An unverified asset requests proximity to your heat source.
quests.discovery: An unknown unit stops at the perimeter of your thermal radius. They display empty hands. 'Thermal sharing requested,' they state.

choices.label: Authorize proximity
choices.outcome_text: You permit entry. They transfer a portion of their caloric reserves and provide updated topographical data for the northern route.
choices.epitaph: Authorized thermal proximity. Acquired updated topographical data.

choices.label: Authorize at maximum range
choices.outcome_text: You assign them the furthest functional radius. Both units maintain readiness. No data is exchanged.
choices.epitaph: Authorized maximum-range thermal proximity. Maintained combat readiness.

choices.label: Deny proximity
choices.outcome_text: You refuse entry. The unit departs, returning to suboptimal thermal conditions.
choices.epitaph: Denied thermal proximity. Contact returned to suboptimal conditions.

choices.label: Execute preemptive strike
choices.outcome_text: You engage immediately. The unit displays higher-than-expected combat readiness despite thermal degradation.
choices.epitaph: Executed preemptive strike on unverified contact. Contact demonstrated high readiness.

quests.trigger: An unknown asset requests medical intervention on a clear route.
quests.discovery: A unit lies immobile in the transit path, actively losing fluid. They signal for assistance. The total lack of cover suggests a potential ambush vector.

choices.label: Provide comprehensive aid
choices.outcome_text: You expend medical supplies and carry their mass. They integrate into your operation and provide ongoing tactical analysis.
choices.epitaph: Provided comprehensive aid to compromised unknown. Unit integrated into operations.

choices.label: Provide basic triage
choices.outcome_text: You apply standard coagulation protocols and direct them to the nearest known medical facility.
choices.epitaph: Provided basic triage. Directed unit to medical facility.

choices.label: Bypass
choices.outcome_text: You maintain a wide perimeter and proceed. The signaling ceases shortly after.
choices.epitaph: Bypassed compromised unknown. Signaling ceased.

choices.label: Extract immediate assets
choices.outcome_text: You detach their supply pack and proceed. The ambush, if one existed, does not trigger.
choices.epitaph: Extracted assets from compromised unknown. Evaded potential ambush vector.

quests.trigger: An independent logistics asset offers material exchange.
quests.discovery: A scavenger operating a manual transport cart signals a halt. 'Exchange rates are favorable today,' they state, keeping one hand on their sidearm.

choices.label: Execute standard exchange
choices.outcome_text: You meet the stated caloric price without friction. The asset provides the coordinates of a stable trading hub as a bonus.
choices.epitaph: Executed standard exchange. Acquired coordinates for stable logistics hub.

choices.label: Negotiate deficit
choices.outcome_text: You aggressively contest the valuation. The asset yields slightly to expedite the transaction.
choices.epitaph: Negotiated material deficit. Secured minor caloric advantage.

choices.label: Bypass
choices.outcome_text: You signal refusal. The transport cart resumes its operational route.
choices.epitaph: Bypassed mobile logistics node. Conserved material.

choices.label: Requisition inventory
choices.outcome_text: You initiate hostiles and seize the cart. The asset's distress signals are ignored by the sector.
choices.epitaph: Requisitioned logistics inventory via force. Sector ignored distress signals.

quests.trigger: You encounter a pre-adolescent asset separated from its unit.
quests.discovery: A small juvenile occupies a structural ruin, emitting low-volume distress vocalizations. 'My primary attachment figure is absent,' they report.

choices.label: Reunite with unit
choices.outcome_text: You expend significant operational time locating their camp. The family unit registers a permanent positive standing for your faction.
choices.epitaph: Reunited juvenile with primary unit. Secured positive faction standing.

choices.label: Transfer to local authority
choices.outcome_text: You deliver the asset to a functioning settlement's intake officer. The officer logs your ID.
choices.epitaph: Transferred unattached juvenile to settlement intake. Identification logged.

choices.label: Bypass
choices.outcome_text: You lack the caloric overhead to manage dependents. You proceed. The vocalizations fade with distance.
choices.epitaph: Bypassed unattached juvenile. Conserved caloric overhead.

choices.label: Re-allocate asset
choices.outcome_text: You transfer the juvenile to an unsanctioned labor camp. The asset comprehends the destination prior to arrival.
choices.epitaph: Re-allocated juvenile to labor camp. Subject comprehended destination.

quests.trigger: An AWOL combatant requests concealment from their unit.
quests.discovery: A combatant lacking standard insignia emerges from cover, raising empty hands. 'I abandoned my post. Do not broadcast my coordinates,' they request.

choices.label: Maintain concealment
choices.outcome_text: You omit their presence from your logs. In exchange, the combatant provides advanced weapon maintenance training.
choices.epitaph: Maintained concealment for AWOL combatant. Acquired weapon maintenance data.

choices.label: Process tactical data
choices.outcome_text: You extract their unit's patrol routes and deployment status before allowing them to pass.
choices.epitaph: Processed tactical data from AWOL combatant prior to release.

choices.label: Bypass
choices.outcome_text: Their factional disputes are outside your parameters. You proceed without engagement.
choices.epitaph: Bypassed AWOL combatant. Ignored factional dispute.

choices.label: Broadcast coordinates
choices.outcome_text: You flag their location for the pursuing patrol. You receive a standard ration chit as compensation.
